subject: [PATCH for-7.5 1/5] memcg: move memory.high enforcement out of try_charge_memcg()

2026-10-10.patch_summary: This patch refactors the code in try_charge_memcg() by moving memory.high enforcement into a new function called memcg_enforce_high(). This change makes the code easier to read and maintain, while also allowing for more flexibility in handling high memory usage. The new function checks if the current or any of its ancestors are over their respective memory.high limits and takes action accordingly, such as scheduling reclaim or slowing down the task. No functional changes were made.

reviews.author: Harry Yoo
reviews.summary: Identified a missing Signed-off-by: in the patch. Otherwise, LGTM and provided a Reviewed-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
On Sat, Oct 10, 2026 at 02:09:53PM -0700, Shakeel Butt wrote:
> try_charge_memcg() does a lot. It charges the page counters, reclaims
> when a limit is hit, may call the OOM killer, and at the end it checks
> and enforces memory.high. Move the memory.high part into a new function,
> memcg_enforce_high(), so that try_charge_memcg() is shorter and the
> memory.high code is easier to read and change.
> 
> The code and its comments move as they are. The only difference is that
> the new function gets allow_spinning from gfp_mask itself.
> 
> No functional change.
> ---

Missing Signed-off-by: ?

Otherwise LGTM.
Reviewed-by: Harry Yoo (Meta) <harry@kernel.org>

2026-10-12.patch_summary: This patch series moves the enforcement of memory.high out of try_charge_memcg() and into a new function, memcg_enforce_high(). This change aims to make the code easier to read and maintain by breaking down the complex logic in try_charge_memcg(). The new function is responsible for checking if the memory or swap high limits are exceeded and taking action accordingly.
